references.text: Abraham also named a place after the Lord (JHVH Jireh - The Lord sees), just as Moses called the altar 'The Lord is my banner'.
Jacob built an altar and named it El-Elohe-Israel, paralleling how Moses built an altar and gave it a name that honored God.
Jacob built an altar in Bethel, a practice that Moses continues by building altars to remember God's intervention.
The context for the altar-building: the victory over Amalek led Moses to call the altar 'The Lord is my banner'.
Moses built an altar at Mount Sinai, demonstrating his practice of building altars to mark significant events with God.
Gideon built an altar and named it 'The Lord is peace' (JHVH Shalom), just as Moses gave the altar a name that described the Lord's character.
Isaiah speaks of a banner (נֵס) that God gives to those who fear him, linking to the concept of the Lord as a banner.
